zh.title: 航空短訊彙整：美空軍加碼Joby自主貨運機計畫累計承諾近3700萬美元；微風航空新增6個航點並接手精神航空遺留航線
zh.summary: 本期收錄4則獨立消息：美空軍加碼Joby自主貨運機計畫累計承諾近3700萬美元、微風航空新增6個航點並接手精神航空遺留航線、美國空軍處置測試飛行員學校3架A-29C機隊。
body: 本期彙整4則航空短訊，各則為獨立事件。部分內容摘自近期站內報導，原文與來源見文末。

1. 美空軍加碼Joby自主貨運機計畫累計承諾近3700萬美元
Joby航空透過AFWERX獲得美國空軍新增資金，用於自主飛行技術，使美空軍累計承諾接近3700萬美元，後續將在太平洋地區進行更多作戰測試。

2. 微風航空新增6個航點並接手精神航空遺留航線
微風航空未來數月將新增6個航點，延續其連接次要機場與未開發市場的點對點網絡，接手部分精神航空退出後留下的航線，並新增牙買加與多明尼加航點。

3. 美國空軍處置測試飛行員學校3架A-29C機隊
美國空軍因評估不符需求處置3架A-29C；正尋求尾旋訓練替代方案

4. ShieldAI公開自主尾坐式戰機X-BAT001首架試飛載具
ShieldAI公開X-BAT001短片，據信為其自主尾坐式戰機的首架試飛載具；影片顯示寬大機翼、數位迷彩與醒目尾噴口，但ShieldAI尚未說明該機為何以水平姿態展示，也未證實其狀態與構型。

en.title: Aviation briefs: US Air Force adds funding for Joby's autonomous cargo aircraft, taking commitment near $37 million; Breeze Airways adds six new destinations and picks up routes left by Spirit
en.summary: 4 independent updates: US Air Force adds funding for Joby's autonomous cargo aircraft, taking commitment near $37 million; Breeze Airways adds six new destinations and picks up routes left by Spirit; US Air Force Divests Three A-29C Super Tucanos From Test Pilot School.
body: 4 independent aviation updates. Includes excerpts of recent reports, with original reports and sources linked below.

1. US Air Force adds funding for Joby's autonomous cargo aircraft, taking commitment near $37 million
Joby Aviation has received additional US Air Force funding through AFWERX for its autonomous flight technology, bringing the service's cumulative commitment to nearly $37 million, with further operational testing planned in the Pacific region.

2. Breeze Airways adds six new destinations and picks up routes left by Spirit
Breeze Airways will add services to six new destinations in the coming months, extending its point-to-point network between secondary airports and unserved markets, replacing Spirit on a number of routes and adding international destinations in Jamaica and the Dominican Republic.

3. US Air Force Divests Three A-29C Super Tucanos From Test Pilot School
US Air Force divests three A-29C Super Tucanos from Test Pilot School, seeking training alternatives.

4. Shield AI rolls out X-BAT 001, its autonomous tail-sitting fighter
Shield AI has offered a first look at X-BAT 001, believed to be the first flight-test vehicle for its autonomous, tail-sitting fighter aircraft, revealing broad wings, digital camouflage and a prominent engine exhaust.

facts.claim: The US Air Force divested the three A-29C Super Tucano turboprops assigned to its Test Pilot School at Edwards Air Force Base, California, after determining they did not meet requirements.
facts.sourceQuote: The US Air Force has divested the three A-29C Super Tucano turboprops assigned to its Test Pilot School at Edwards Air Force Base, California, after determining that they did not meet the school’s requirements.

facts.claim: An Edwards Air Force Base spokesperson stated that the Air Force is exploring alternatives for spin training and mission systems instruction.
facts.sourceQuote: The spokesperson said the Air Force was now exploring alternatives for spin training and mission systems instruction.

facts.claim: On October 29, 2026, the Air Force Test Center posted a notice of intent to award Sierra Nevada Company a basic ordering agreement for on-call maintenance and ground handling of the three aircraft.
facts.sourceQuote: In a notice of intent posted on SAM.gov on October 29, 2026 , the Air Force Test Center said it plans to award Sierra Nevada Company (SNC) a sole-source, firm-fixed-price basic ordering agreement for on-call maintenance and ground handling of the three aircraft.

facts.claim: The planned maintenance contract includes ground tasks such as repairing leaks and towing, but explicitly excludes return-to-flight maintenance and airworthiness restoration.
facts.sourceQuote: The work covers repairing fuel, hydraulic, and oil leaks, replacing tires, and towing the aircraft around the base. Return-to-flight maintenance and airworthiness restoration are excluded.

facts.claim: Delivered by Embraer and SNC, the aircraft were originally acquired by Air Force Special Operations Command before being transferred to Edwards Air Force Base in July 2024.
facts.sourceQuote: The aircraft, delivered by Embraer and SNC , were originally acquired by Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) for its Combat Aviation Advisor mission but were divested after the command’s requirements changed, according to the 412th Test Wing.
